question: Should experimental Claws be allowed to create globally shared stdio MCP declarations, and if so what host-authorized command broker and ownership/tenancy contract must apply before merge?
rationale: This is a new core authority over executable and remote MCP configuration; source inspection can identify unsafe behavior, but only maintainers can choose whether the feature belongs in core and what permanent authorization model is acceptable.

options.title: Pause for RFC and broker design
options.body: Keep this stacked slice unmerged until the RFC defines a host-authorized shared-MCP model and the branch implements it.

options.title: Approve a scoped core model
options.body: Explicitly sponsor a core lifecycle owner, but require allowlisted/brokered stdio commands, per-owner authorization, and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Use an extension-owned path
options.body: Move optional MCP bundle ownership to the existing plugin/skill ecosystem if no missing core API remains after the RFC review.

recommendation.title: Pause for RFC and broker design
recommendation.body: Keep this stacked slice unmerged until the RFC defines a host-authorized shared-MCP model and the branch implements it.
